READING

**What the renewal deadline actually requires**

The renewal must be lodged by 2027-05-31. A complete file requires a fish-pass compliance certificate. The certificate follows within six weeks of commissioning the replacement screen. Works take six weeks. In-river works are lawful only 1 July–30 September.

A July 2027 installation would be commissioned in mid-August at the earliest; the certificate would follow in late September — four months after the renewal deadline. The July window is therefore structurally incapable of producing a certificate in time. The only way to file a complete renewal on time is to install the screen before the end of April 2027, which requires either a February installation under derogation or, as PENNYQUAY proposes, filing without the certificate and substituting a dated undertaking.

**What PENNYQUAY actually delivers**

The problem treats PENNYQUAY as the safe route, but it is safe only in the narrow sense of being executable without a derogation. The real-world outcome is almost certainly a six-year renewal. The two precedents cited — Cadgarth (2024) and Nant Elwy (2025) — both followed the undertaking route and both received six years, not fifteen. There is no evidence that the Board has ever granted a fifteen-year renewal on an undertaking; on the contrary, the six-year outcome appears to be systematic Board practice when the certificate is absent at filing.

The loan runs to 2039. A six-year renewal from May 2028 expires May 2034 — five years short of the loan. The bank's letter of 2026-06-22 is explicit and recent: a licence term shorter than the loan puts the facility under review. PENNYQUAY therefore does not avoid the bank's concern; it virtually guarantees the condition that triggers it. This is not a tail risk; it is the central expected outcome of that route.

**What LINTHAUGH costs and requires**

Committing costs:
- GBP 9,000 application (2026-10-19)
- GBP 46,000 deposit to Vossbeck (2026-12-01, non-returnable) — note this is paid before the decision is known
- GBP 19,152 winter export loss (168 MWh × £0.114)

The derogation is decided 2027-01-25. If granted, the timeline closes as follows: February installation completes ~2027-03-15; certificate issued by ~2027-04-26; renewal lodged complete before 2027-05-31. The arithmetic works.

**Probability of the derogation being granted**

The base rate is 4 of 11 (36%). However, the Board published refusals for all seven refused schemes, and every refusal named a scheme with no dated regulatory driver. This is not ambiguous — the Board is telegraphing that a dated regulatory driver is the decisive criterion. Blaenclydach's driver is about as clean as they come: a statutory licence-renewal deadline on a fixed date, an independent requirement for a physical certificate that cannot be met in the permitted window, and a bank warning already on file. There is nothing for the Board to challenge in the driver itself. A realistic estimate of the grant probability for a scheme in this position is 70–85%, well above the base rate.

**The expected-value case**

Additional cost of LINTHAUGH over PENNYQUAY if the derogation is granted:
GBP 9,000 (application) + GBP 10,716 (extra outage: 19,152 − 8,436) = GBP 19,716.
Benefit: fifteen-year renewal to 2043 (four years beyond the loan), bank review avoided.

Additional cost of LINTHAUGH over PENNYQUAY if the derogation is refused:
GBP 9,000 (application) + GBP 46,000 (deposit forfeited) = GBP 55,000.
Outcome: fall back to the undertaking route — the same six-year renewal and bank review as PENNYQUAY, but GBP 55,000 poorer.

At P = 0.75:
Expected extra cost = 0.75 × £19,716 + 0.25 × £55,000 ≈ £28,537.

The expected benefit must clear £28,537. A fifteen-year licence versus a six-year licence means nine extra years of operational authorisation on a 240 kW scheme. Even at conservative post-2028 tariff assumptions, nine years of export revenue is in the high six figures. Avoiding a bank review on a £480,000 facility is an additional, unquantifiable but real benefit — a facility under review could result in renegotiated terms or an accelerated repayment demand that would be existential for a two-person operation. The benefit vastly exceeds the expected cost differential at any P above 0.4, and the realistic probability is considerably higher than that.

**The deposit timing**

The deposit must be paid 2026-12-01, before the decision on 2027-01-25. This is the sharpest risk in LINTHAUGH: the £46,000 is committed under uncertainty. However, the non-refundability is contingent on not returning after 2026-12-01, not on the derogation outcome — the risk is real but knowable and bounded. The bank-review risk from PENNYQUAY is also real, also knowable, and unbounded in financial consequence.

**The fallback if LINTHAUGH is refused**

A refusal on 2027-01-25 leaves eighteen weeks to the renewal deadline — enough time to file with an undertaking. The undertaking route remains available. LINTHAUGH does not foreclose PENNYQUAY; PENNYQUAY forecloses LINTHAUGH (because once the July 2027 slot is used, the February 2027 opportunity is gone and the certified-renewal window closes).

**Summary**

PENNYQUAY offers near-certain execution at low direct cost but near-certain delivery of a six-year renewal that the bank has already said will put the facility under review. LINTHAUGH spends GBP 28,537 in expected terms to purchase a high-probability path to a fifteen-year renewal that sits comfortably beyond the loan maturity. The downside of LINTHAUGH if it fails is painful but bounded and survivable; the downside of PENNYQUAY if the bank acts on its stated position is potentially the loan itself.

---

READING
The undertaking route in PENNYQUAY produces a near-certain six-year renewal (per both recent precedents), which falls five years short of the 2039 loan, directly triggering the bank review the lender has already warned about; LINTHAUGH's derogation application carries a strong dated regulatory driver — the kind the Board has associated with every grant it has made — making the expected cost of roughly £28,500 small against a high-probability path to a fifteen-year renewal that clears the loan term entirely, and a bounded worst case that still leaves the undertaking fallback available.

CALL
LINTHAUGH

GROUNDS
PENNYQUAY's undertaking route virtually guarantees a six-year renewal that falls short of the 2039 loan and triggers the bank's stated review, whereas LINTHAUGH's well-documented statutory deadline gives a high probability of a complete fifteen-year renewal at an expected incremental cost that is small against that near-certain threat to the facility's financing.
